chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, while I was listening, about a man who made upon himself to walk to the House of God and the sacrificial offering.

He said: And he swore by every solemn oath that he would never speak to his father, nor testify in his favor, nor would he ever eat with him at the table, nor would a roof shelter both him and his father ever.

He said: Then he was silent. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Does anything remain?' He said: 'No, may I be your sacrifice.' He said: 'Every oath of cutting off kinship ties is nothing (i.e., such oaths are void).'

key_terms.الْمَشْيَ إِلَى بَيْتِ اللَّهِ: Walking to the House of God (Ka'bah) — a vow of pilgrimage on foot, considered a highly meritorious religious act
key_terms.الْهَدْيَ: The hady — sacrificial animal brought during hajj or as part of a vow
key_terms.قَطِيعَةِ رَحِمٍ: Cutting off kinship ties — one of the major sins in Islamic ethics, the severance of family relations
key_terms.لَا جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be your sacrifice — a formulaic expression of reverence and self-sacrifice used when addressing the Imam
key_terms.يَمِينٍ غَلِيظٍ: A solemn/weighty oath — the most binding form of oath, sometimes invoking God's attributes

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about oaths that involve cutting off family ties?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal question posed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) concerning a man who made comprehensive oaths vowing to sever all ties with his father, including refusing to speak to him, testify on his behalf, share a meal, or share a roof. The Imam's ruling is incisive: any oath whose fulfillment requires severing family ties (qati'at al-rahim) is void and carries no legal weight. This ruling reflects a foundational principle in Shia jurisprudence that oaths binding one to haram actions — such as cutting family ties, which is among the grave sins — are themselves nullified.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Amro Bin Al Bara’a who said, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked, and I was listening, about a man who made upon himself to walk to the House of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the sacrifice’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And he swore with every harsh oath, ‘I shall not speak to my father, ever, nor shall I testify for him goodly, nor shall he eat with me upon the table, ever, nor will I and him share the roof of a house, ever’.

Then he was quiet. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Does there remain anything?’ He said, ‘No, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Every cutting-off of a relationship, so it is not with anything’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Amr ibn al-Bara’ who has narrated the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked, when I was listening, about the case of a man who has made obligatory upon himself to walk to the House of Allah and the offering animal,
he has taken an oath in all severity not to ever speak to his father, testify about anything good for him. Never eat with him on one table or live with him under one roof.

He then remained quiet. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asked, ‘Is anything else left?’ He replied, ‘No, I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘All manners of cutting relation with relatives is nothing (not permissible).”’
